David Arul Raj @ David vs D.Arul Kamaraj on 25 March, 2024 
Author: T.V.Thamilselvi
Bench: T.V.Thamilselvi
 Crl.O.P.N
 In The High Court Of Judicature At Madras
 Dated : 25.03.2024
 Coram
 The Honourable Mrs.Justice T.V.Thamilselvi
 Crl.O.P.No.28020 of 2022
 and Crl.M.P.No.17228 of 2022
 David Arul Raj @ David .
 Vs.
 D.Arul Kamaraj ..
 Prayer: The Criminal Original Petition filed under Section 482 of
 Cr.P.C., to call for the records in connection with C.C.No.143 of 2
 the file of Judicial Magistrate-II, Tambaram and quash the same.
 For Petitioner : Mr.S.Mohideen
 For Respondent : No appearance
 Order
This Criminal Original Petition has been filed to call for records in C.C.No.143 of 2021 on the file of the learned Judicial Magistrate-II, Tambaram and quash the same. 
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 2. The respondent filed a private complaint before the learned Judicial Magistrate-II, Tambaram against the petitioner for the offence punishable under Section 420 of IPC. Based on that complaint,
the learned Magistrate took cognizance of the case in C.C,No143 of 2021. Challenging the said complaint, the petitioner has approached this Court to quash the proceedings. 
3. The learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that originally, the petitioner was tenant under the respondent and there was dispute in respect of tenancy, however, he paid the rent regularly from 2017 onwards. Further, the terms of agreement also modified. Subsequently, September 2020, the David Arul Raj @ David vs D.Arul Kamaraj on 25 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/38555878/
1 petitioner has vacated the premises and he shifted his shop to other place. Further, the learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the respondent has given a false complaint as if the petitioner involved in unlawfully activities and violated the Government order during Covid -19 even after 9.00 p.m., to 11.00 p.m., he sold the foods. He further submitted that there was civil dispute between them https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis and there is no criminal offence made out against this petitioner and now, the case was transferred to the learned Judicial Magistrate, Pallavaram, in C.C.No.516 of 2023. Further, the learned counsel for the petitioner has relied on by Judgment in Neetu Singh & Others Vs.State of U.P. (2022 Live Law(SC) 281.
4. Inspite of notice given to the respondent, there was no representation.
5. On a perusal of the records, it reveals that the petitioner has produced the rental agreement as document on the side and also notice was issued by the Food Safety Officer but all the allegations in the petition is vexatious one. Further, the petitioner has handed over the premises to the respondent and shifted his business to other place, due to some dispute, the respondent has given a false complaint against the petitioner with some ulterior motive. Therefore, the trial Court has taken on file in C.C.No.143 of 2021 is erroneous one. Now, the case was transferred to the learned Judicial Magistrate, Pallavaram, in C.C.No.516 https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis of 2023. Further, on considering the records, it reveals that there is no prima facie materials against the petitioner involved in unlawfully activities with dishonest intention the part of the petitioner, hence there is no criminal offence is made out Therefore, this Court is of the view that the dispute is civil in nature,
thus Civil dispute has been given criminal colour. Hence, this Court is inclined to quash the proceedings in C.C.No.516 of 2023 pending on the file of the learned Judicial Magistrate,
Pallavaram.
6. In the result, this Criminal Original Petition is allowed. Consequently, connected miscellaneous petition is closed. No costs.
